title: Nex AGI Nex model family

reading.body:
Nex AGI replaced its entire Nex line on 2026-09-08, retiring both June models and shipping two successors the same day.

The pattern is a full generational swap rather than an addition. Nex-N2-Pro and Nex-N2-Mini, released 2026-06-08 and 2026-06-24, are both marked delisted with an expiry of 2026-09-08, the same date the N2.5 pair arrived. The two surviving versions keep identical context and output limits, 262144 and 235929 tokens, and both accept text and image input. What changed is price: the new Mini holds the old Mini's rates at $0.03 input and $0.1 output per million tokens, while the new Pro costs $0.08 and $0.25 against the old Pro's $0.25 and $1.

For AI specifically, the relevant fact is that every version in this family publishes open weights, and the tokenizer is Qwen3. Open weights at these prices mean the models can be run outside a hosted API, which shifts the cost of serving them from per-token billing toward the compute and power someone has to supply. The data does not say what hardware that requires, so it cannot be read as a statement about data center demand.

The limits are real. There are no benchmark rows, so nothing here measures quality, and no parameter counts are given, so the size of the open-weight releases is unknown. Two versions and one tokenizer describe a narrow family, and the catalog covers only what OpenRouter lists.

family_reading.text: Nex AGI Nex is a small family, with two versions in the catalog, both released on 2026-09-08. Every version publishes open weights, and both support reasoning. Both accept image and text input and return text. The context window is 262144 tokens across the family, with a maximum output of 235929 tokens. Pricing is low: Nex-N2.5-Mini costs $0.03 per million input tokens and $0.1 output, while Nex-N2.5-Pro costs $0.08 input and $0.25 output. The facts suggest the family suits long document or image plus text work where open weights and reasoning matter, at modest cost. Limits are the narrow version spread, only two tiers, and no benchmark rows are named, so measured quality is not shown here.
